instruction: Replace all commas with semicolons in the train record document using Find & Replace.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to remove duplicate train IDs from a docx file using a Python script via terminal. The script had a syntax error. Agent then tried selecting text and highlighting, but never successfully modified the document content.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, find files, install pip packages, write Python scripts with python-docx, navigate LibreOffice Writer, select text, use formatting tools
metadata.failure_analysis: Python script had syntax errors in heredoc string escaping. Model got confused after script failure and resorted to highlighting text instead of fixing the script.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a basic Find & Replace operation - one of the most fundamental Writer operations. The model showed familiarity with keyboard shortcuts and menus.
metadata.explanation: Task requires replacing all commas with semicolons in the document. Getter reads saved docx and counts comma/semicolon occurrences. Metric checks: no commas remain (0.5), semicolon count equals 300 (0.3), first line has 4 fields with semicolons (0.2).

scoring_breakdown.no_commas: 0.5 - No commas remain in the document
scoring_breakdown.correct_format: 0.2 - First line has 4 fields separated by semicolons

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the saved docx file and counts old (comma) and new (semicolon) delimiter occurrences, which is the right state to extract for verifying a find-and-replace operation.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule' by directly accessing expected.get('expected_new_delimiter_count', 300) without wrapping in rules.
Coverage is complete: checks (1) all commas removed (0.5), (2) correct semicolon count (0.3), (3) first line structure preserved with 4 fields (0.2), totaling 1.0.
Postconfig properly activates the Writer window and saves the file with Ctrl+S before the getter reads it, preventing stale state issues.
Partial credit logic is reasonable: tolerance of ±5 on semicolon count gives 0.15 partial credit, accommodating minor edge cases.
Minor concern: the expected_new_delimiter_count of 300 is a hardcoded value that cannot be independently verified without the source document data.
Minor concern: the first-line 4-field check assumes a specific document structure that may not generalize, though it is reasonable for this specific document.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider documenting how the expected_new_delimiter_count of 300 was derived (e.g., from manual inspection of the source document) to improve verifiability.
Consider adding a comment in the metric about the assumption that the first line of the document has exactly 4 comma-separated fields.
